# Forecast-weather experiment: NYISO N.Y.C. day-ahead price (generated by scripts/evaluate_forecast_weather.py)

**Question.** The earlier backtest's best model used the target day's ACTUAL temperature (a perfect-foresight oracle). Does weather still help when only a day-ahead FORECAST is available?

**Setup.** Same walk-forward protocol and frozen XGBoost hyperparameters as `results/backtest_report.md` ({'max_depth': 4, 'n_estimators': 300}, chosen on 2022 only using the oracle feature set C; not retuned for forecast weather). Weather = GFS (`gfs_global`) 2 m temperature from the Open-Meteo Previous Runs API issued 1 day (primary) or 2 days (sensitivity) before the valid hour. 23 test days (2023-12-29 to 2024-01-20) have a missing forecast hour (one upstream outage) and are excluded for every model below; 709 days / 17,004 hourly points remain, identical for all models. Nothing is imputed and actuals never fill forecast gaps.

**Variants.** (a) trained on ACTUAL temperature, predicted with the forecast; (b) trained on archived FORECASTS. The control is the no-weather model B retrained on exactly the dates (b) can train on.

**Limits.** One zone, one weather point, GFS only, one 2-year window, one frozen hyperparameter set. The run initialisation time behind `previous_day1` is undocumented, so the 2-day-lead rows are the leakage-safe check. No gas, outage or generation-mix data. A retrospective backtest, not a trading result.

## Forecast quality (test days, hours with both forecast and actual)

| lead | MAE (deg C) | bias | RMSE | hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 day | 1.75 | +0.75 | 2.24 | 17,028 |
| 2 day | 1.85 | +0.71 | 2.36 | 17,004 |

## Overall (all models on identical points; rMAE reference = yesterday-naive)

| model | MAE ($/MWh) | RMSE | bias | rMAE vs yesterday-naive |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Naive: same hour yesterday [reference] | 5.78 | 13.14 | +0.17 | 1.000 |
| Seasonal naive: same hour last week | 12.42 | 30.03 | +2.05 | 2.148 |
| XGBoost B (prices+calendar+load), no weather, full history | 5.78 | 12.72 | +1.23 | 0.999 |
| XGBoost B, no weather, trained on the same dates as forecast-trained models [control] | 6.14 | 13.00 | +1.78 | 1.063 |
| XGBoost + forecast temp (1-day lead), (a) trained on actual temp | 4.72 | 10.35 | +0.11 | 0.816 |
| XGBoost + forecast temp (1-day lead), (b) trained on forecasts | 5.35 | 10.76 | +1.81 | 0.924 |
| XGBoost + forecast temp (2-day lead, sensitivity), (a) trained on actual temp | 4.71 | 10.33 | +0.03 | 0.815 |
| XGBoost + forecast temp (2-day lead, sensitivity), (b) trained on forecasts | 5.36 | 10.65 | +1.82 | 0.926 |
| XGBoost + target-day ACTUAL temp (oracle, upper bound) | 4.77 | 10.43 | +0.70 | 0.824 |

|---|---|---|---|

| XGBoost + forecast temp (1-day lead), (a) trained on actual temp | -1.057 | -4.71 | 2.54e-06 |
| XGBoost + forecast temp (1-day lead), (b) trained on forecasts | -0.429 | -1.55 | 0.122 |
| XGBoost + forecast temp (2-day lead, sensitivity), (a) trained on actual temp | -1.063 | -4.70 | 2.66e-06 |
| XGBoost + forecast temp (2-day lead, sensitivity), (b) trained on forecasts | -0.420 | -1.31 | 0.189 |

## Selected pairwise comparisons (first model minus second; negative = first is better)

| pair | mean daily MAE difference | DM stat | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|
| xgb_D1_train_actual vs xgb_B_matched_window | -1.422 | -4.90 | 9.72e-07 |
| xgb_D1_train_fc vs xgb_B_matched_window | -0.793 | -3.31 | 0.000934 |
| xgb_D1_train_actual vs xgb_B | -1.054 | -4.40 | 1.06e-05 |
| xgb_D2_train_actual vs xgb_D1_train_actual | -0.005 | -0.29 | 0.775 |
| xgb_C_oracle_temp vs xgb_D1_train_actual | +0.049 | +0.78 | 0.435 |

With 707 serially correlated daily losses, treat p-values as indicative.
